Class MainRegionLayout

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.core.MainRegionLayout
public final class MainRegionLayout extends Object
Movement ③ — the custom-screen layout resolver. A custom screen names ONE main panel = its frame (centred on the screen window, exactly like a vanilla container's menu frame); every other panel anchors to that frame with a MenuRegion via RegionMath.resolveMenu(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int, int) — the SAME math vanilla-injected panels take against the menu frame. So the relative verbs (rightOf / above / below) and their edge-unaware Tree layout are retired for custom screens, and siblings get region anchoring + screen-edge clamping (no panel renders off-screen) + the single overlay rule (①) for free.

Coordinate convention

The result's bounds are leftPos-relative (the main panel sits at (0,0)), matching what the screen's render + slot-positioning code adds leftPos/topPos to. The main frame's screen origin is the returned leftPos/topPos, so a vanilla container's leftPos + slot.x math keeps working unchanged.

What each non-main panel becomes

  • Overlay (Panel.isOverlayPositioned() — center(), or a dim/modal panel): floats centred on the screen window (the single overlay rule ①). NOTE: MKCHandledScreen renders its panels in declaration order — there is no separate on-top/dim pass for an overlay added directly to a custom screen's panel list (none exist today; injected modals use the vanilla region path, which DOES have the 3-pass). Wiring an on-top pass here is a follow-up if an in-panel custom-screen overlay is ever needed.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.REGION: anchored to the main frame via its MenuRegion, clamped into the screen safe area. Siblings sharing a region stack with RegionConstants.MENU_STACK_GAP.
  • PanelPosition.Mode.SCREEN_ANCHOR: pinned to a screen corner (chrome like a Back button), independent of the frame.

Note (②). Size comes from the screen's sizeFn (which factors in custom-screen slot groups, not just panel elements), and the origin from RegionMath.resolveMenu(MenuRegion, ScreenBounds, int, int, int, int, int), whose screen-edge clamp keeps siblings on-screen. Per-sibling auto-SCROLL (the full ② treatment) is a slot-group ↔ scroll integration not yet wired on this path — siblings that exceed their region are clamped over the frame rather than scrolled. Inert for fitting siblings.

    • hasMain

      public static boolean hasMain(List<Panel> panels)
      Whether panels contains a PanelPosition.Mode.MAIN panel — the gate for using this resolver vs the legacy BODY-stack layout.

    • resolve

      public static MainRegionLayout.Result resolve(List<Panel> panels, Function<Panel,int[]> sizeFn, int screenW, int screenH, boolean reserveTitle, boolean autoFitMain)
      Resolves the main-panel frame + region-anchored siblings.
      Parameters:
      panels - the screen's panels (declaration order — siblings sharing a region stack in this order)
      sizeFn - per-context Panel → {outerWidth, outerHeight} (padding-inclusive)
      screenW - GUI-scaled screen width
      screenH - GUI-scaled screen height
      reserveTitle - reserve a title strip at the top of the frame (true for container screens that draw the title at the frame top; false for standalone screens that draw it at the screen top)
      autoFitMain - feed the MAIN frame a vertical budget so it auto-scrolls when taller than the screen ("shrink-to-fit is the default", applied to the frame itself). Pass false for a slot-bearing container main — its vanilla slots are pinned in absolute coords and have no scroll hook, so it must keep its natural height. Standalone (element-only) mains always pass true.
